text: The following question stood in the name of  Miss Cheng Li Hui –  6 To ask the Minister for Education (a) whether there are coordinated efforts between the career centres of Institutes of Higher Learnings and agencies such as Enterprise Singapore to connect graduates with enterprises to provide employment opportunities; (b) how can graduates be further supported in their endeavour to secure employment and also further their academic pursuits and retraining to better equip them for the post-COVID economy; and (c) how can internship opportunities play a role for graduates during this challenging period.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Fresh graduates are entering the job market at an exceptional time.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Many will face challenges in securing a job.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The Institutes of Higher Learning or IHLs, together with various Government agencies, will provide whatever support we can to all graduates entering the workforce.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Second, the IHLs, namely the Autonomous Universities, Polytechnics and ITE – each have a significant network of companies and employers.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: They have been leveraging them to provide internships and Work-Study programmes.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Employers in general are facing difficulties due to COVID-19.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But many are still prepared to hire and others who do not have job vacancies may be prepared to offer traineeships.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: To ensure that graduates have access to these jobs and opportunities, the IHL Career Centres will continue to provide career guidance and assistance, labour market information and organise career fairs.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The Career Centres have stepped up the intensity of their efforts this year, including using online outreach and counselling tools to support graduates remotely.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: For graduates who decide to delay their entry into the job market, the IHLs will support them to learn new skills and knowledge.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: In that way, graduates can take up this programme and delay their entry into the labour market while doing something very meaningful.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Graduates can also enrol for further studies, including Advance Diplomas, Specialist Diplomas and graduate certification programmes.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This has become a challenge as many internships have been disrupted due to COVID-19 and our circuit breaker measures to curb community spread.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: IHLs are working hard to identify alternatives so as to mitigate any impact on learning outcomes and graduation timings.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: COVID-19 will be a defining moment in our graduates’ lives, especially this batch of graduates.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: I urge our graduates to rise to the occasion and use this crisis to bring out the best of their generation.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The Government will support them as closely as possible as they enter the next phase of their life’s journey.
